subject.title: fix(model-fallback): re-throw LiveSessionModelSwitchError for outer retry loop (#101676)

question: Should this external PR wait for contributor-supplied real active-turn live-switch proof, or may maintainers accept the synthetic fallback proof plus source review as sufficient?
rationale: Repository policy treats external PR real behavior proof as a merge gate for user-visible runtime behavior, and automation cannot prove the contributor's live setup for them.

options.title: Require real switch proof
options.body: Ask for redacted live output, logs, terminal transcript, or a short recording showing an active turn retrying on the requested model before merge.

options.title: Accept a proof override
options.body: A maintainer may intentionally merge on code review and synthetic coverage while owning the remaining live-runtime proof gap.

options.title: Pick a canonical candidate PR
options.body: If maintainers prefer the sibling implementation, close or pause the other candidate only after the chosen PR is proven and ready.

recommendation.title: Require real switch proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted live output, logs, terminal transcript, or a short recording showing an active turn retrying on the requested model before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc owns the closest recent fallback redirect history and is the best available routing candidate for the proof-sufficiency choice.
